newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GINOLA WONDER GOAL ILLUMINATES NEWCASTLE VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GINOLA WONDER GOAL ILLUMINATES NEWCASTLE VICTORY.

text.p: David Ginola scored one of the season's great goals as Newcastle outclassed Ferencvaros of Hungary 4-0 to reach the third round of the UEFA Cup 6-3 on aggregate on Tuesday.
The Frenchman struck after Colombian Faustino Asprilla had sewn up the tie with a goal in each half and prompted Newcastle manager Kevin Keegan to say afterwards: "That was our best performance yet."

The goal, which put Newcastle 3-0 ahead, came after 65 minutes. Ginola, lurking on the edge of the penalty area, trapped a loose ball on his right thigh, teed it up with the inside of his right foot, and blasted a high, sizzling, left-foot volley into the top left-hand corner of Jozef Szeller's net.

Newcastle, playing without world record signing Alan Shearer, recovering from a groin operation, could have won by an even bigger margin but Peter Beardsley missed a first-half penalty and Newcastle wasted a number of scoring chances before Asprilla eventually made the breakthrough just before halftime.
England striker Les Ferdinand wrapped up the victory with a last-minute goal.
But another England international had a night to forget.

Inter-Milan's Paul Ince was sent off in extra time for a second bookable offence as Inter, bidding to win the UEFA Cup for the third time in seven seasons, struggled to get past unfancied Casino Graz. The tie finished 1-1 on aggregate before Inter won 5-3 on penalties.

Inter goalkeeper Gianluca Pagliuca thanked team mate and Swiss international Ciriaco Sforza after the match for stopping a goal-bound shot at full-stretch on the line in the last minute after Pagliuca was beaten.
But Valencia's goalkeeper Andoni Zubizaretta was not so lucky -- sent-off for hand-ball outside the penalty area five minutes into the second half against Slavia Prague .
But his Valencia side held on to draw 0-0 to reach the third round of a European competition for the first time in eight years. They went through 1-0 on aggregate.
There were no major shocks overall, although Germans Schalke were made to fight all the way for their place in the last 16 by Trabzonspor of Turkey.
Schalke went to Trabzonspor 1-0 ahead from the first leg and quickly raced into a 2-0 lead on the night thanks to two headers from Dutchman Johan de Kock, which put them 3-0 ahead over the two legs.
But Trabzonspor fought back, going 3-2 up on the night through two goals from Hami Mandirali and causing some concern to the Germans who were then leading only on the away goals rule.
With 15 minutes remaining, Martin Max, who scored the only goal in the first leg, clinched the tie with Schalke's third.
Fellow Germans Hamburg and Karlsruhe joined Schalke in the next round, although Borussia Moenchengladbach were eliminated 4-3 on aggregate despite winning 1-0 at Monaco.

Hamburg, 3-0 ahead on aggregate against Spartak Moscow, drew 2-2 in Russia to win 5-2 on aggregate, while Karlsruhe, also 3-0 up from the first leg, lost 2-1 at Roma where Abel Balbo scored twice in five minutes for the home side, but went through 4-2 on aggregate.
Espanyol scored a 1-0 win over Dutch side Feyenoord in Rotterdam but never looked like pulling back the 3-0 deficit they suffered on their own ground in the first leg.
Arteaga gave the visitors some hope with a ninth minute opener, but they could not find the net again.
